title: Count Distinct Numbers Not in Banned List
hints: the numbers you're choosing from live in a small conceptual range [1, n] - you don't actually need to build an array of size n to reason about which are banned
put the banned values into a hash set for O(1) membership checks, since only those matter, not the whole range
greedily walk candidate values starting from 1 upward. skip anything in the banned set, and for everything else keep a running sum, stopping the moment adding the next number would exceed maxSum
since n can be up to 10^9 but banned is small, make sure your loop terminates based on maxSum and banned.length, not by literally iterating up to n every time
commonMistakes: forgetting to ignore banned values that are outside the range [1, n]
not deduplicating the banned list, which can cause incorrect skipping logic
iterating all the way to n even when maxSum is reached far earlier, causing a timeout on large n

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of `banned` integers, an upper bound `n`, and a
`maxSum`. Consider the integers from 1 to `n`, excluding any that appear
in `banned`.

**Greedily pick as many distinct numbers as possible from what remains, always preferring smaller numbers first, such that the total of everything you picked does not exceed `maxSum`, and return how many numbers you were able to pick.**
constraints: banned may contain values outside [1, n], which should simply be ignored
notes: every number from 1 to n is banned (answer 0)
maxSum is smaller than the smallest available number (answer 0)
banned contains duplicates or values greater than n

sampleTestCases.explanation: available numbers in order are 2, 3, 4 (1 and 5 are banned). pick 2 then 3, total 5, cannot add 4 since 5+4=9 > 6
only 8 is available (1 through 7 are banned). pick 8, total 8 <= 18
available numbers are 1..6 (11 is out of range). pick 1, 2, 3, total 6, cannot add 4

optimal.pattern: same greedy scan, but treat the banned values like markers over the bounded range [1, n] rather than materializing the whole range, so it scales even when n is huge

bruteForce.approach: iterate from 1 to n, skip banned numbers using a hash set lookup, and keep adding to a running sum and count until the next number would exceed maxSum
bruteForce.time: O(n) to build the set and scan
